cards.front: Recall a key point about Spartan Society & the Helots
cards.back: Spartan society was organised around military preparedness; full citizens (homoioi/equals) were professional soldiers supported by helot labour

cards.front: Recall a key point about Spartan Society & the Helots
cards.back: The agoge was the rigorous state education system that trained Spartan boys from age 7 in discipline, endurance and warfare

cards.front: Recall a key point about Spartan Society & the Helots
cards.back: Helots were the enslaved population of Messenia who farmed the land; they vastly outnumbered citizens and were constantly controlled by fear

cards.front: Recall a key point about Spartan Society & the Helots
cards.back: The krypteia was a secret police of young Spartans who terrorised and killed helots to prevent rebellion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Spartan Society & the Helots
cards.back: Spartan government: two hereditary kings (military and religious roles), five ephors (overseers with wide powers), Gerousia (council of 28 elders) and the apella (citizen assembly with limited power)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Spartan Society & the Helots
cards.back: Spartan women had more freedom than in other Greek cities: they owned property, trained physically and managed households while men were in barracks
